newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil ends firm buoyed by German demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil ends firm buoyed by German demand.

text.p: NWE gas oil ended higher on Friday as IPE benchmark futures pushed tentatively higher and underlying physical demand remained strong, traders said.
The Oct IPE contract settled $2.25 higher at $221.75 a tonne.
On the heating oil barge market, premiums were boosted to Oct IPE +$8/+$9 fob ARA for second half delivery by a flurry of demand from Germany.
"The market's very nervous, but a lot of those who are short are stocking up before the weekend in case the Iraqi situation escalates. It's a real lottery," one trader said.

There was some confusion over where low sulphur barge premiums stood. Some traders insisted premiums on winter quality 0.05 percent were as high as Oct IPE +$17/+$18 fob ARA, while others put them at closer to Oct IPE +$12/+$14. On the cargo market, heating oil was the focus of the market traders. "Given the stocks situation and the pick-up in German demand the market would be strong with or without the situation in the Gulf," one trader said.
Russian remained in demand as German buyers in search of 0.2 percent snapped them up. Premiums were at Oct IPE +$7/8 and some traders said they looked set to strengthen due to thin demand.
